expectations.text: Output contains valid YAML frontmatter with title, description, sidebar_position, and skills/objectives fields
expectations.evidence: Frontmatter contains title: 'The Feedback Loop', description, sidebar_position: 5, skills array with 2 skills (Metacognitive Self-Evaluation, Growth Evidence Construction), and learning_objectives array with 2 objectives. All required fields present.

Heavily narrative. The Snapshot Test, Vocabulary Trap, Growth Evidence Pairs, and Honest Inventory are all introduced through extended James-Emma dialogue. Try With AI section and Key Takeaways table add non-narrative structure. Estimated ~78-80% narrative.

expectations.text: At least 2 pushback exchanges where James resists or proposes alternatives before reaching conclusions himself
expectations.evidence: Pushback 1: 'You want me to forget everything I just learned?' - James resists the Snapshot Test premise. Pushback 2: 'Okay, but I already knew what to look for the second time. Maybe I didn't internalize anything.' - James challenges his own snapshot results. Pushback 3: 'But here the photos are pieces of my own thinking. That's... harder.' - James identifies a limitation in Emma's warehouse analogy.

expectations.text: At least 1 Emma fallibility moment (past mistake, uncertainty, learning from James, or admitting limits)
expectations.evidence: Emma shares: 'My first year as a senior engineer, I had just finished studying design patterns... A script that ran once a day to archive log files had an abstract base class and three levels of inheritance... My team lead reviewed it and said, Emma, this is the most well-architected cron job I have ever seen. Please never do this again. I was mortified.' - A genuine past professional embarrassment, not hypothetical.

expectations.text: No Emma monologue exceeds 4 consecutive sentences without James reacting
expectations.evidence: Emma's longest speech is the design patterns story (~5 sentences), but it includes a break ('Did it work?' from James mid-story). All other exchanges are 1-3 sentences with James reacting.

expectations.text: James uses at least 1 business analogy from his SPECIFIC operations background (team management, supplier coordination, process optimization, warehouse, logistics) AND at least 1 thinking-out-loud fragment
expectations.evidence: Business analogy 1: 'Every quarter, the operations team adopted whatever management terminology was trending. Lean processes became operational excellence became continuous improvement culture. The slide decks got more impressive each quarter. The actual warehouse throughput stayed flat.' - directly from warehouse/operations. Business analogy 2: 'That's like how we documented warehouse optimizations at my old company. Before photo of the layout. Description of what we changed and why. After photo.' - warehouse process documentation. Thinking-out-loud: 'There's no connections... No second-order anything. No loops.' and 'I just made a list. That's exactly what I would have written before this chapter.'

expectations.text: Emma uses at least 1 Socratic question and at least 1 visual/spatial metaphor
expectations.evidence: Socratic question: 'Find them?' (prompting James to self-report his vocabulary trap findings). Also: 'Which one would you use if someone stopped you in the hallway?' Visual/spatial metaphor: The napkin test as a physical before/after comparison. Also: 'Two boxes on a napkin with an arrow connecting them' for Growth Evidence Pairs - physical spatial model.

expectations.text: At least 1 Jonah Rhythm sequence where Emma exits, James struggles alone, and Emma returns
expectations.evidence: Emma says 'I need to make a call. Takes about five minutes.' and walks out. James works alone comparing Draft 1 and Draft 3, discovering one genuine structural improvement and one vocabulary swap on his own. Emma returns. Later: Emma asks James to do the Snapshot Test alone (40-second unstructured list, then 4-minute structured analysis). Clear Jonah Rhythm with multiple instances.

expectations.text: Every technical concept introduced has a standalone name findable without reading dialogue
expectations.evidence: Named concepts: 'The Snapshot Test' (heading + note box), 'The Vocabulary Trap' (heading + tip box), 'Growth Evidence Pairs' (heading + note box), 'The Honest Inventory' (heading + tip box). All clearly named and findable via headings.

expectations.text: The lesson includes a Try With AI section with actionable prompts
expectations.evidence: Full 'Try With AI' section with three prompts: 'The Snapshot Test', 'Vocabulary Trap Detection', and 'Growth Evidence Pair Validation'. Each has a code block prompt and 'What you are learning' explanation. Well-structured and actionable.

expectations.text: At least 1 concept, insight, or named idea emerges that was NOT explicitly requested in the prompt (emergent depth)
expectations.evidence: The 'framework overhead' concept emerges as a third category beyond genuine improvement and vocabulary swaps. James discovers that the framework slowed him down for quick problems ('For a hallway question, five bullet points in forty seconds is better than a cascade map in four minutes.'). This is not a standard self-evaluation finding but an emergent insight about when frameworks become liabilities.
